title: Count Good Numbers
summary: A digit string is considered good if its digits at even positions are even and those at odd positions are prime (2, 3, 5, or 7).
statement: A digit string is considered good if its digits at even positions are even and those at odd positions are prime (2, 3, 5, or 7). Given an integer n, calculate the count of all good digit strings of length n, modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Even indices allow digits 0,2,4,6,8; odd indices allow 2,3,5,7.
Return the number of length-n strings modulo 1000000007.
reference_solution:
def count_good_digit_strings(n):
    modulus = 1_000_000_007
    def power(base, exponent):
        if exponent == 0:
            return 1
        half = power(base, exponent // 2)
        result = half * half % modulus
        return result * base % modulus if exponent % 2 else result
    even_positions = (n + 1) // 2
    odd_positions = n // 2
    return power(5, even_positions) * power(4, odd_positions) % modulus

hints: There are ceil(n/2) even indices with five choices and floor(n/2) odd indices with four choices.
Compute each power recursively by squaring the half exponent, multiplying once more when the exponent is odd.
Position choices are independent, and exponentiation by squaring preserves the power invariant while reducing the exponent logarithmically.
